synthesis.text: On the evidence provided, the theme is defined by three member claims, of which only kramasadbhava:v3 is specified. That claim establishes that the powers have a support, namely the great Lord, and that the flashing has an order-less support rather than being the order itself; this is required by the structure of ordered experience. The claim is said to introduce the support on which the following argument depends, and its function is limited to establishing the local support, not every claim about the universal Self. Because the contents of kramasadbhava:v1 and kramasadbhava:v4 are not given, the theme can only be said to be constituted by their membership as DEFINES plus the specified v3 content.
synthesis.crux: The load-bearing point is kramasadbhava:v3's introduction of the support: the flashing is not the order itself but has an order-less support, the great Lord, and this is required by the structure of ordered experience. The conclusion that the verse establishes the support of the powers depends on this introduced support; if it were removed, the argument would have no support.
synthesis.unresolved: The contents of kramasadbhava:v1 and kramasadbhava:v4 are not provided, so how they contribute to the theme beyond being listed as DEFINES remains unspecified. The term 'akrama' remains uncertain, and the claim's boundary excludes every claim about the universal Self, so the theme's relation to such claims is unresolved.

synthesis.text: The claims jointly establish, for candidate theme 1, that the verses v1, v3, and v4 all define a single theme: the support of the powers. The shared explanation is that the flashing (pratibhā) is not the order itself; rather, it has an order-less support, the great Lord, and this support is required by the structure of ordered experience. The theme is thereby established as a local claim about this support, not as an essay-level thesis, a cross-tradition comparison, or a modern application. Because all three verses play the same DEFINES role with identical content, the theme rests on the repeated establishment of this local support of the powers.
synthesis.crux: The load-bearing point is that the verse introduces the support and that the following argument depends on it; the conclusion that the verse establishes the support of the powers is derived from this introduction. The commitment is underdetermined by the uncertain term akrama, and it is bounded to establishing the local support, not every claim about the universal Self.
synthesis.unresolved: The precise meaning of akrama remains uncertain, so the nature of the order-less support is not fully determined by these claims.

synthesis.text: The verse establishes the support of the powers: the flashing (pratibhā) is not the order itself, has an order-less support, the great Lord (with akrama, uncertain), and this support is required by the structure of ordered experience—within the local claim boundary, not as every claim about the universal Self.

crux.what: The load-bearing commitment is that the flashing has an order-less support, the great Lord.
crux.why: The conclusion depends most on this premise; if it fails, the other premises only describe the flashing's relation to order and cannot establish the support of the powers.

synthesis.unresolved: Whether akrama should be read as an order-less support rather than as a mere description of the flashing's own order-less nature; if the latter, the verse would only describe the flashing's nature and would not establish a distinct support for the powers.
synthesis.boundary: It establishes the local support, not every claim about the universal Self.
